1: Some devotees worship you, constantly yoked in this way, and others worship the imperishable, the unmanifest. Which of them know yoga best?
2: Those who fix the mind on me and worship me, always yoked and endowed with supreme faith: I hold them to be the most yoked.
3: But there are those who worship the imperishable, the indefinable, the unmanifest, which goes everywhere and is unthinkable, unchanging, unmoving and fixed.
4: Restraining the whole group of the senses, of even buddhi everywhere, and delighting in the welfare of all beings, they reach me alone.
5: The trouble is greater for those whose minds are attached to the unmanifest, for the unmanifest goal is painful to reach for those who have bodies.
6: But there are those who lay down all actions in me and hold me as the highest, who worship me, meditating on me by a yoga that has no other object at all.
7: Their minds are fixed on me, son of Pṛthā, and before long I become the one who lifts them out of the ocean of death and wandering on.
8: Place your mind on me alone and let buddhi enter into me. From then on you will dwell in me alone. Of this there is no doubt.
9: But if you cannot settle the mind steadily on me, then seek to reach me by the yoga of practice, winner of wealth.
10: If you are unable even to practise, make action for me your highest aim. Even by doing actions for my sake you will reach perfection.
11: And if you cannot do even this, then take refuge in my yoga and, with the self restrained, give up the fruit of all action.
12: For knowledge is better than practice, meditation is better than knowledge, and giving up the fruit of action is better than meditation. Peace follows at once from giving up.
13: There is one who hates no being at all, who is friendly and compassionate, free of the sense of mine and the sense of I, the same in pain and pleasure, and patient.
14: Always content, a yogī with the self restrained and of firm resolve, with mind and buddhi offered to me: such a person, devoted to me, is dear to me.
15: One from whom the world does not shrink, and who does not shrink from the world, who is free from joy, impatience, fear and agitation: that one too is dear to me.
16: One who expects nothing, who is pure, skilled, sitting apart, with distress gone, who gives up all undertakings and is devoted to me: that one is dear to me.
17: One who does not rejoice or hate, grieve or long, who gives up the auspicious and the inauspicious and is full of devotion: that one is dear to me.
18: There is one who is the same toward an enemy and a friend, and likewise in honour and dishonour, the same in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, and free from attachment.
19: Blame and praise are equal to such a person, who is silent, content with anything whatever, without a home, of steady mind and full of devotion: that person is dear to me.
20: But those who honour this nectar that accords with dharma, just as it has been spoken, who have faith, hold me as the highest and are devoted: they are exceedingly dear to me.
